blindSummary: Not individually flagged by the country dossier in any respect: no region-specific law, incident, ordinance or enforcement finding was identified for this region either way (and it is not one of the regions the dossier's legislative-inventory note enumerates). No facility, expression or assembly restriction exists outside the national framework anywhere in the country; the 2023 national trans-equality law is implemented by the regional government; a 2026 national report found 44% of LGTBI respondents had experienced a hate-motivated incident. The dossier's general notes place this region in the sparsely-populated interior where LGBT-visible community life is thinner than in the big cities.
blindSourceSummaries: Official state-gazette publication of the country's trans-equality law of 28 February 2023 (published 1 March 2023): a national law establishing real and effective equality of trans people and guaranteeing the rights of LGTBI people, whose administrative and education-facing provisions are implemented by the sub-national governments - the framework this region applies.

International human-rights organisation news release (16 February 2023) welcoming the country's new gender-recognition law: legal gender recognition by self-declaration from age 12 under certain conditions without medical diagnosis, placing the country among the earliest self-declaration jurisdictions alongside a small set of other early adopters; frames diagnostic and sterilisation requirements elsewhere as rights violations.

Criminal-defence law-firm analysis (June 2026, updated September 2026) disentangling three frequently conflated statutes: the 2023 trans-equality law is an ordinary statute that never amended the criminal code (its content is civil, administrative, health, employment and educational); the discrimination aggravating factor and the hate-offences provisions in the criminal code come from a 2022 reform (hate offences: 1 to 4 years' imprisonment plus a 6-12 month fine); 'gender expression' appears in no article of the criminal code.
